candidate_findings.title: Drag/drop mutations are not bound to shared-buffer save authority
candidate_findings.gap: The direct copy, overwrite, move, and delete path is not defined as a typed buffer transaction and has no arbitration contract for an open or dirty source/destination buffer.
candidate_findings.why_it_matters: An imported overwrite can coexist with stale in-memory content that later saves over it; a moved or deleted file can retain an editor tab with an obsolete save target; split panes, undo history, diagnostics, search/index state, Git state, and chat/review links can disagree about the authoritative file.
candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The capsule does not specify the transaction source, dirty-buffer conflict state, destination overwrite precedence, path remap or tombstone behavior, or completion propagation to file watchers, index/LSP consumers, Source Control, previews, and path-bearing chat/review consumers.

evidence_refs.excerpt: The editor buffer transaction model is explicit: user edits, preview edits, agent writes, FileSafe/LSP edits, restore/revert actions, and recovery replay all enter the shared buffer through typed transaction sources before dirty state, undo grouping, and save authority are updated.

Save authority remains single-owner per file path: one shared buffer, one dirty flag, one last-saved version, and one authoritative save/retry path across split panes, preview surfaces, LSP apply-edit, and agent mutation flows.

candidate_findings.missing_or_underspecified: The security boundary for link targets, link-bearing directory trees, link replacement after validation, and follow-versus-no-follow behavior of every downstream consumer is absent; the phrase "paths outside project" is also ambiguous because legitimate incoming sources are intentionally outside the project.

#### 1.1.3 Gaps and how we address them

| **Drop target when tree is scrolled** | The drop target is the **row under the cursor** at drop time, not the "selected" row. Tree must hit-test the cursor to the correct row (folder or root) when the drop occurs. |

| **Symlinks** | When **copying in**, AutoDecision: copy the symlink as a symlink (do not resolve). When **copying out**, the OS typically resolves; we provide the path. When **moving out**, deleting the source removes the symlink, not the target. |
| **Read-only or locked files** | If copy or delete (move) fails because the file is read-only or locked, show the error and do not overwrite. Optionally offer "Try again" or "Skip." |
| **Very long path** | If the resulting path exceeds OS limits (e.g. 260 chars on Windows), fail with a clear message ("Path too long") and suggest moving the project or shortening names. |

| **Drag from within the same project** | Default to **copy within project** so external drag/drop and in-project drag/drop share the same conflict model. Holding **Shift** switches the operation to **move within project** (copy then delete source). Same rules as external drop; no special case unless we add "reorder" semantics later. |

| **Accessibility** | Keyboard alternative: e.g. "Paste from clipboard" (paste files from clipboard into selected folder) and "Copy path to clipboard" (so user can paste elsewhere). Screen reader: announce "Drop target: {folder path}" when hovering over a valid target. |
